definition: Insertion sort grows a sorted prefix by taking the next element and inserting it into the position where it belongs. Nearly sorted input is cheap, because each element only moves a short distance. The worst case, reverse-sorted input, compares every pair.
details: It is often used for the tiny partitions inside a faster sort.

complexity.time: O(n^2) worst and average. O(n) when the input is already sorted.

examples: Cleaning up a list that is already almost in order
